signals.text: Part B: Co-curricular music This is about opportunities for pupils to sing and play music, outside of lesson time, including choirs, ensembles and bands, and how pupils can make progress in music beyond the core curriculum.

Children are encouraged to read widely from the library, selecting from a range of authors and genres, and all children are read with regularly to ensure they also have a book on the correct reading band to reflect their age, stage, ability and phonics sounds focus.
All readers have access to a reading scheme which is designed for KS2 progression, but all children are assessed when they come to Guillemont and our SSP Read, Write, Inc.

Reading is taught through whole class sessions, we teach our children key reading skills referencing the content domains from the KS2 English Reading Test Framework and apply these to high quality texts that are chosen for progression across the year groups.

Information
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Provision at Guillemont
At Guillemont Junior School we welcome all children and follow the local authority admissions guidance for children including those with additional needs. All staff and governors share the responsibility to ensure that the needs of all pupils are met within our school.
Miss Natasha Solway is our Inclusion Lead and oversees the provision for all pupils with SEND across the whole federation. In addition, her role is to oversee the provision for Looked After Children/Previously Looked After Children, children with English as an additional language, children with other vulnerabilities and children who are Talented / Academically more able. Mr Matthew Phillips is our Mainstream SENDCO and Ms Ellie Kearsley is our Resourced Provision(s) Manager. To contact them, please phone the office on 01252 666846 or email them using the following email address: admin.guillemont@pags.co.uk
The provision (what we are able to offer) at Guillemont is given in the SEND Information Report. The Local Authority requires all school to issue their provision for children with SEND. Please click on the link below for our Send Information Report (Special Educational Needs)
Follow the link below to access further information regarding the services for children and young people with SEN and/or disabilities within Hampshire – click here.
SENDIASS
The new Hampshire SENDIASS can be contacted via the website: www.hampshiresendiass.co.uk; email: hampshiresendiass@coreassets.com or telephone: 0808 164 15504
Transport
If your child has a Statement or EHCP, you may be able to apply for transport to and from the school. Please click here for a link to the ‘Home to School Transport (HCC). You will need to click on the ‘down arrow/chevron’ on the ‘Local Offer’ line for the information about home to school transport.

Enrichment
Residential Visits
Our residential programme is rooted in character building. By stepping outside of their comfort zones, children learn how to challenge themselves, work collaboratively and develop confidence in unfamiliar situations. Whether it is spending a first night away from home, tackling outdoor activities, studying geography in the field or taking part in team-building challenges, pupils are encouraged to discover strengths they may not yet realise they possess.
The residentials are closely linked to our five core school values:
At Guillemont Junior School, we believe that education is about much more than academic achievement alone. Our residential visits support our vision of giving children “The Roots To Grow, The Wings To Fly” by helping them to become confident, capable and compassionate young people who are prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond school.
The 2024/25 Residential Visits
This academic year (2024/25) we are offering a residential experience to all children.
Yr3 a one night sleep-over camp on the school field, campfire and games – Friday 6th June 2025 – Saturday 7th June 2025.
Yr4 a three days, 2 nights ‘Viking experience’ at Ufton Court (Near Reading) – Wednesday 6th – Friday 8th November 2024.
Yr5 a four night five day residential visit to Swanage. Field trip to study coastal geography – Monday 12th – Friday 16th May 2025.
Yr6 a four night five day residential visit to Grittleton House – Monday 7th – Friday 11th July 2025.
Please visit our ‘Parent Workshop’ webpage for the latest presentations linked to the residentials’.

Teaching & Learning
English - Reading
Intent
At Guillemont, through reading and listening to a range of rich, diverse texts, children develop in a range of ways: culturally, emotionally, intellectually, socially and spiritually. Children are able to read easily, fluently and with good understanding in order to become confident communicators, who are ready to participate fully in society and their next phase of learning. We value reading so highly that children leave with a habit of ‘reading for pleasure’ and will be self-motivated to acquire new knowledge that builds on what they already know.
Implementation:
Teaching of Reading is based upon the National Curriculum and the new Reading Framework 2023 and teachers ensure that this is enhanced to ensure children have the best possible outcomes. Guided Reading lessons take place every day for 40 minutes and children are read to during lessons and story time. The English Curriculum leader keeps up-to-date with developments in the subject by regularly attending the HIAS run district Core Provision meetings as well as the annual English conference; information from these sessions is passed onto staff through workshops. HIAS advisers are invited into school on INSET days to provide training for teachers and LSAs when a need arises.
Reading is taught through whole class sessions, we teach our children key reading skills referencing the content domains from the KS2 English Reading Test Framework and apply these to high quality texts that are chosen for progression across the year groups. Comprehension and the reading skills aren’t taught explicitly, but are embedded in the lessons, so that children build on key skills. Every week, children hear adults reading, and spend time on fluency activities based on their quality text. Scaffolding is provided to remove barriers to reading, and challenges are presented to all children to extend their thinking.
Children are encouraged to read widely from the library, selecting from a range of authors and genres, and all children are read with regularly to ensure they also have a book on the correct reading band to reflect their age, stage, ability and phonics sounds focus. Our library has been recently refurbished, and we have a librarian on staff to manage and look after the stock of books and ensure they are regularly updated. We subscribe to School Library Service who regularly audit our book stock (in the library and in classes) to ensure books are new, relevant and enticing, and provide extra services such as class e-books and can attend workshops for staff training . Story time is timetabled twice a week to ensure that a love of reading is shared. All readers have access to a reading scheme which is designed for KS2 progression, but all children are assessed when they come to Guillemont and our SSP Read, Write, Inc. (Freshstart for the upper school) is taught to support those children who have fallen behind. Reading regularly at home is encouraged through a whole school incentive, BoomRead is used as an online record for children, parents and teachers can monitor reading at home and at school. Bug Club is available to all children at school and at home and provides an alternative online format.
Reading for pleasure is embedded as a culture throughout the school, adults model good reading practice. Reading for pleasure is encouraged to be intrinsically incentivised – as children build on their reading skills and reading miles, so they will recognise their achievements and develop a love for reading. Other incentives throughout the school include celebrating World Book Day, an Author Visit, National Poetry Day, with a visit from a poet, Reading Cafes, shared reading, sponsored reading opportunities to win prizes and raise money to spend on books, a Class Reading Cup in assemblies and prizes for activity on BoomRead. Each class has a quiet library session timetabled to ensure each class gets regular exclusive time in the library. We are also creating Reading Boxes to take outside, and if children do not have books at home we provide them through SLS and a charity run by staff in the school. We endeavour to instil a love of poetry across the school: a ‘Poem of the Week’ is distributed to read and display with ideas and activities to explore further.
Our school has a clear focus on the development of speech and language. We have implemented tiered vocabulary development throughout the curriculum and use working walls, visual prompts (WIDGET) and pre teach vocabulary. This helps children to make links and develop their speaking and listening as well as their reading. Barriers to learning are addressed in Guided Reading lessons and children are given scaffolds as appropriate to ensure they can access the curriculum.

Teaching & Learning
Music
Intent
At Guillemont Junior School we believe music is inclusive and accessible to all. We expose our children to different instruments, composers, genres and cultures. We inspire our children to be creative and have a love of learning by exposing them to stimuli and teaching using high quality examples that are performed via live experiences or technology. As musicians, children will learn about the different dimensions in music and are able to plan, practice, perform and evaluate their own and others’ work. They will work independently and collaboratively, to understand notation; feel confident performing with instruments or using their own voice; and share their work and skills with others. There is a clear learning journey across all of the four year groups that ensures there is progression in skills and knowledge and that children remember and retrieve prior learning over time.
Implementation:
At Guillemont Junior School the music curriculum consists of: a timetabled music lesson each week; a weekly singing assembly, where singing skills are taught and refined by a range of teachers, so that the children are exposed to a wide range of singing styles; a whole year group, high quality, sustained performance either at Christmas or the end of year 6; performances in class assemblies or end of project celebrations; exposure to a wide range of composers/ musicians/genres/ cultures along with appropriate historical references. Music is also taught in parallel with other subjects such as Dance and Science. Over the last year we have provided many opportunities for children to listen to musicians virtually and aim to invite musicians into school for live performance where possible. We have visited local and national venues to hear and work with orchestras such as the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and Grange Opera, rather than listening virtually as we feel interaction with musicians is a vital skill and learning experience. There are established links with Hampshire music service to enrich the music provision at our school.
We offer extra-curricular opportunities to sing in the choir and take part in Young Voices at the O2 London or sing at local music festivals. Children can also have specialist instrumental lessons on recorder, drums, piano and ukuleles. There is an expectation for children to share knowledge and expertise of their instruments to benefit and inspire other pupils.
Lessons show children progress from Year 3 to Year 6, they use a variety of instruments with care for expression, effect, accuracy and creativity and use their voices with an increasing awareness of tune, tone, pitch and harmony,. Pupils have the opportunity to grow in skills including listening, recognising, reproducing, composing, performing, conducting, leading and reflecting. Children are making links in their learning in other subjects and to the Guillemont Core values and are able to work and perform alone and in a group, having an awareness of others working in groups and teams. Teachers are skilled at asking questions to push learning forward, reason and improve or address misconceptions.
Music schemes of work show how children will gain knowledge, remember and retrieve key facts, master skills, plan, prepare and perform. They build on previous knowledge and skills to ensure each child progresses during their time with us from their various starting points. All lessons are inclusive to allow all to succeed and children will be supported through teacher guidance, reducing cognitive load or Widget Online symbols.
Impact:
We strive to ensure that our children‘s attainment is in line with or exceeds their potential when we consider their varied starting points.

Mental Health and Well-being
Everyone has ‘mental health’ and this can be thought of in terms of:
Being mentally healthy is also about having the strength to overcome the difficulties and challenges we can all face at times in our lives – having the confidence and self-esteem to be able to take decisions and to believe in ourselves.
At Guillemont, we believe it is important to raise the profile of how to look after our mental health and wellbeing. There are many ways we support children with their mental health and wellbeing in school, and we have recently established a Community and Wellbeing group, where ambassadors across year 3 to year 6 have been chosen to be advocates for mental health in young people. We are happy to talk to you about any concerns to do with your child’s mental health or well being.
